# Ranolazine

**Authors:** Mirembe Reed, Shwetha Gopal, Preeti Patel, Diala Nicolas

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Ranolazine is an antianginal agent approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of chronic stable angina in ischemic heart disease. The drug is used as an adjunct to standard therapies such as antiplatelet agents, beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, nitrates, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers, and statins to reduce angina frequency and improve functional capacity. Ranolazine exerts its therapeutic effect primarily by inhibiting the late inward sodium current, thereby reducing intracellular calcium overload and myocardial wall tension without significantly affecting heart rate or blood pressure.
